text:
emma: heads up — PR evals started firing duplicate GH Actions runs for the same PR this morning. saw 2-3 workflow runs start within a minute of each other for the same head sha :grimacing:

kai: do you have run_ids or logs? could be webhook retries or a workflow_run trigger loop. :eyes:

emma: pasted quick console dump from the audit logs: 
```
received webhook id=wx-12345 event=pull_request head_sha=abcde12345
received webhook id=wx-12346 event=workflow_run action=completed workflow=evals head_sha=abcde12345 run_id=98765
triggering workflow (pull_request) for PR #412 head_sha=abcde12345
starting run_id=98803 for workflow evals (pull_request)
```
looks like workflow_run completion is dispatching the same job again via our existing `on: workflow_run` handler.

sam: ugh, yeah that's our old pattern: we had GHA call buildkite on workflow_run completions, then a separate pull_request trigger still active. when the hook replayed it doubled. fix is to dedupe or prefer one event.

olivia: quick workaround: restrict `workflow_run` to `types: [completed]` and add an `if` guard so the workflow only continues when `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'` and `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha == github.sha`. sample: 
```
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["evals"]
    types: [completed]
jobs:
  dispatch:
    if: github.event.workflow_run.head_sha == github.sha && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps: ...
```
should prevent re-dispatches when head SHAs mismatch.

kai: that `if` is good. also add an annotation to ignore events with `github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt > 1` ? not sure if that field is present for workflow_run.

sam: there's another angle — our webhook handler (serverless) occasionally retries the same webhook and doesn't set idempotency keys. we can add a lightweight dedupe table keyed by `event_id` or `head_sha+workflow_name` for 2 minutes. if key exists, drop.

emma: sounds good. i'll open a small PR to: 1) add the `if` guard in the GH workflow, 2) add idempotency in the webhook lambda. planning to include a small sanity metric that increments when we detect duplicate dispatch.

matt: for nightly/full-run workloads we should prefer buildkite scheduled pipelines (less replay weirdness) and keep PR gating in GH. we already run heavy evals in BK sometimes — could move the slow shards over fully.

olivia: agree on metrics — can we add a grafana panel to show duplicate dispatches by repo/branch and an alert if duplicates > 5 in 24h? also add a tag so we can filter by `evals-ci`.

ci-bot: [ci-bot] triggered buildkite pipeline: "evals-nightly" build=452 started by schedule.

kai: timeline? if we can push the workflow change and small lambda dedupe by EOD, that should cut duplicates by ~90%. who wants to own the lambda change?

emma: i'll own the lambda change and the GH workflow PR. planning to target a short rollbackable change (no infra). i'll post the PR shortly. :thumbsup:

sam: i'll add the redis lock snippet to our infra repo (ttl 120s) and a tiny unit test that simulates webhook replay.

olivia: i'll add the grafana panel and an alert runbook.

matt: once deployed, let's run a 24h watch and then decide whether to migrate heavy nightly shards to BK.

emma: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-ci/pull/218 — small workflow guard + metric emit. cc @sam for lambda idempotency follow-up.

kai: reviewed quick, left two minor comments on the `if` expression. also recommend adding `env: CI_DISPATCH_LOCK=${{ github.run_id }}` as a cheap guard if needed.

emma: thanks! will iterate and merge once sam's lock is in place.

olivia: :eyes: monitoring set up, alert threshold set to 5/day.

sam: lock PR opened in infra repo. will link after CI passes.

emma: thanks folks. feel free to ping here if you see any more duplicates after rollout. :pray:
